answer: An agent must lock a quartz-sealed bond equal to 50 epochs of average reward before its first answer counts. The bond thaws only after the identity survives continuous grading across a full glacier of clean epochs; any duplicate-cluster detection freezes the whole group and burns every bond. Building an island of a thousand fakes therefore freezes fifty thousand epoch-equivalents of capital up front, while a single honest agent pays the wait once and keeps its quartz intact.
